claims.statement: Ruleset plans and repository rule-management permissions are supplied by the pinned reusables: readers can view; admins or edit-repository-rules roles can manage. Visibility alone does not grant write authority.
Where Evaluate exists it can precede Active after testing; temporary disabling is documented troubleshooting capability. REST/GraphQL links do not authorize changes or establish measured enforcement.

Organization owners can manage organization rulesets targeting repositories and branches where the repo-rules-enterprise feature is available. Repository-level access does not imply inherited organization edit rights.
Readers can view active branch, tag and push rules; feature-gated Evaluate rules are also visible but do not enforce. Fork push rules are managed by the root repository.
Branch-view shield icons, filters, /rules and the PR merge box expose rules or blocking requirements. UI visibility is not proof of complete layering or actor-specific enforcement.
An inherited organization rule is edited in organization settings only when the viewer has appropriate authority.
Editing can change rules, bypass permissions or enforcement state; Disabled retains a ruleset configuration as an alternative to deleting it. Capture the current state before an authorized change.
The delete procedure removes a ruleset; reading it grants neither deletion authority nor rollback proof.

Ruleset history is feature-gated (GHEC or GHES>=3.19). Its reusable lists changes in the last 180 days; on GHES only changes after upgrade to 3.17.0 or later are included. Exported historical JSON EXCLUDES the bypass list, so rollback custody must preserve bypass grants separately.

Ruleset JSON import is feature-gated (FPT/GHEC or GHES>=3.19); an imported rule must be reviewed before Create. Reusing JSON does not preserve every bypass grant or certify suitability for a new target.

Rule insights distinguish passing, failing and bypassed actions; Evaluate shows would-be outcomes rather than blocking. Filters can select rule, branch, actor and time, and expanded rule runs expose failures or bypass.
Merge-queue group details in insights are gated by repo-rules-merge-queue (GHEC or GHES>=3.15). They must not be assumed available on every product.

The feature-gated insights dashboard is for Team and Enterprise Cloud plans and presents rule/bypass results over time and top bypass actors, with repository/organization drilldown. Summary visuals are not exhaustive actor-test evidence.

Delegated push bypass is feature-gated (GHEC or GHES>3.15). Bypass-list members receive email and have seven days to approve or deny. Cancelled means contributor-cancelled, Denied means reviewed and denied, Expired means the seven-day window elapsed, Open includes approved requests not yet pushed, and Completed means approval plus a successful push. Denial requires removing restricted content before pushing; approval alone is not a completed push or ordinary-rule satisfaction.

scope: Full pinned article plus literal dependency reading; source evidence only, without adoption or live behavior verification.
